title: Research on Correlation of PSLE-based School Placement and Socio-economic Status Performance Gap
what_it_is: Research on Correlation of PSLE-based School Placement and Socio-economic Status Performance Gap

sections.label: PSLE placement and SES gap
sections.summary: Ministry has not studied and does not plan to study whether PSLE-based secondary school placement amplifies the socio-economic performance gap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education regarding the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) findings linking earlier academic sorting to stronger socio-economic status (SES) performance associations (a) whether the Ministry has assessed whether PSLE-based school placement at age 12 amplifies the SES-performance gap; (b) if so, what that assessment found; and (c) if no such assessment exists, whether the Ministry intends to conduct one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: We have not studied, nor do we plan at this time to study, whether secondary school placement based on the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) results amplifies this skew, as there are many factors that influence the academic performance of our students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Instead, our focus is to help all our students achieve their full potential, regardless of background.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This includes providing more support to students from more disadvantaged backgrounds and also providing porosity in our education pathways, such as through Full Subject-Based Banding at the secondary level, to strengthen their education outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Especially since these indicators can give us a sense of whether the measures that have been undertaken by MOE are working.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor this trend closely as part of our overall efforts to ensure that all of our students are able to maximise their full potential.

sections.label: Review and public engagement
sections.summary: The Ministry is reviewing the matter and will engage the public in education conversations, updating when ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: On the Member's second question, we are reviewing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: We will also engage the public in our education conversations, and update when ready.

sections.label: Primary school academic intervention
sections.summary: Primary schools provide targeted academic intervention, including learning support, reading remediation and mathematics support, for students needing help with foundational skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: For instance, primary schools do provide very targeted academic intervention for students who need more support to strengthen their foundational skills in reading, literacy and numeracy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: This includes learning support programmes, reading remediation programmes and learning support for mathematics.
